eligibility_reason: This is a Reproducibility Project: Cancer Biology Replication Study that reports completed replication experiments, with new bacterial cultures and a new cohort of germ-free Il10-/- mice, of experiments published in Arthur et al. (2012, Science) ('we attempted a replication of the experiments reported in Figure 4A-F, and Supplemental Figure 7 and 10 of Arthur et al. (2012)'). Results and a meta-analysis against the original are reported, so it is scoreable.

effects.original_authors: Arthur, JC; Perez-Chanona, E; Mühlbauer, M; Tomkovich, S; Uronis, JM; Fan, TJ; Campbell, BJ; Abujamel, T; Dogan, B; Rogers, AB; Rhodes, JM; Stintzi, A; Simpson, KW; Hansen, JJ; Keku, TO; Fodor, AA; Jobin, C
effects.replication_study: Protocol 1 / Figure 1 — in vitro bacterial growth assay (replication of Supplemental Figure 7 of the original)
effects.outcome: In vitro growth of E. coli NC101 vs the isogenic pks-deficient NC101Δpks strain (growth curves and intrinsic doubling time)
effects.timepoint: not applicable: growth curve read every 30 min over a single overnight culture; no designated follow-up timepoint
effects.description: The original reported that deleting the pks pathogenicity island does not affect E. coli NC101 growth in vitro, the two isogenic strains showing equivalent growth curves and similar doubling times (~53 min for NC101, ~64 min for NC101Δpks).
effects.citation_sentence: This is comparable to what was reported in Supplemental Figure 7 of Arthur et al. (2012) and described in Protocol 1 in the Registered Report (Eaton et al., 2015).
effects.evidence: Results and discussion, 'Impact of pks island deletion on bacterial growth': "Similar to the original study, NC101 and NC101Δ pks growth curves were visually equivalent to each other (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplement 2), indicating deletion of pks does not affect E. coli growth in vitro." and "To summarize, for this experiment we found results that were similar to the original study."
effects.notes: This is an original NULL claim (pks deletion has no effect on growth) and the replication also finds no effect and calls the results 'similar to the original study' -> success under the codebook's null-claim rule. Enumeration caveat for the adjudicator: a second coder might treat the growth assay as a strain-validation/control experiment and give it no row; I include it because the original reported it as a result (Supplemental Figure 7) and the Registered Report designated it as a replication protocol in its own right. No meta-analysis was possible ('the original study reported a single growth curve for both strains'), and the original NC101 doubling time fell outside the replication's 95% CI while the NC101Δpks value fell inside it — the authors nonetheless summarize the experiment as similar.

effects.original_title: Intestinal inflammation targets cancer-inducing activity of the microbiota
effects.original_authors: Arthur, JC; Perez-Chanona, E; Mühlbauer, M; Tomkovich, S; Uronis, JM; Fan, TJ; Campbell, BJ; Abujamel, T; Dogan, B; Rogers, AB; Rhodes, JM; Stintzi, A; Simpson, KW; Hansen, JJ; Keku, TO; Fodor, AA; Jobin, C
effects.replication_study: Protocol 3 / Figure 2 — AOM-treated germ-free Il10-/- mouse survival (replication of Supplemental Figure 10 of the original)
effects.outcome: Overall survival of AOM-treated germ-free Il10-/- mice mono-associated with NC101 vs NC101Δpks
effects.timepoint: 18 weeks after mono-association (the original study's endpoint; used for the direct comparison and the meta-analysis). The replication's own prespecified endpoint was 18 weeks after the last AOM injection.
effects.description: The original reported that absence of the pks island had a small, but not statistically significant, effect on survival of AOM-treated germ-free Il10-/- mice (NC101 75%, 9 of 12; NC101Δpks 62.5%, 5 of 8 surviving to 18 weeks after mono-association).
effects.citation_sentence: To test whether absence of the pks island reduced tumorigenic potential, but not inflammatory potential of E. coli, we attempted to independently replicate an experiment similar to the one reported in Figure 4A–F, and Supplemental Figure 10, of Arthur et al. (2012).
effects.evidence: Results and discussion, Figure 2 / 'Meta-analyses of original and replicated effects': "When considering only the survival data up to 18 weeks after mono-association, which is the timing performed in the original study, we found results that were in the same direction as the original study." and "Both results are consistent when considering the direction of the effect, that death occurred more often in mice mono-associated with NC101Δ pks compared to NC101, with both effect size point estimates falling within the confidence interval of the other study. A meta-analysis (Figure 4) of these effects resulted in a HR of 1.92, 95% CI [1.11, 3.30], which was statistically significant (p = 0.0188)".
effects.notes: Coded success because this is the one effect the authors were able to compare and combine: the replication effect (HR 1.95, 95% CI [1.10, 3.45], exploratory log-rank p = 0.0230 over the original's timeframe) is in the same direction as the original (HR 1.69, 95% CI [0.31, 9.09]), each point estimate lies inside the other's CI, and the random-effects meta-analysis is significant. Competing readings an adjudicator should weigh: (a) the original's survival difference was NOT statistically significant while the replication's (exploratory) analysis was, so a coder applying the 'original claimed no effect' rule could call this a failure; (b) the replication's own prespecified analysis (18 weeks post-AOM, log-rank p = 0.0608) was not significant and the matched-timeframe analysis was exploratory and run after a timing error was discovered during peer review, which could support inconclusive. The authors' explicit statements ('in the same direction as the original study', 'Both results are consistent') are the basis for success.

effects.replication_study: Protocol 3 / Figure 3A — macroscopic tumor number (replication of Figure 4A-F of the original)
effects.timepoint: Mice surviving 14 weeks or more after the last AOM injection (original study assessed 18 weeks after mono-association)
effects.description: The original reported that mono-association with NC101 produced enhanced tumor multiplicity relative to the isogenic pks-deficient strain, absence of the pks island giving a statistically significant decrease in macroscopic tumor burden (estimated median count: NC101 = 8, NC101Δpks = 2) without an impact on tumor size.
effects.citation_sentence: To test whether absence of the pks island reduced tumorigenic potential, but not inflammatory potential of E. coli, we attempted to independently replicate an experiment similar to the one reported in Figure 4A–F, and Supplemental Figure 10, of Arthur et al. (2012).
effects.evidence: Results and discussion (Figure 3A): "The median count in sections in which individual tumors were detectable for NC101 mono-associated mice was 3.5, which was greater than in NC101Δ pks mono-associated mice (median count of 2). Because individual tumors could not be distinguished, tumor counts cannot be directly comparable to the original study where the absence of the pks island resulted in a statistically significant decrease in macroscopic tumor burden (estimated median count: NC101 = 8, NC101Δ pks = 2), without an impact on tumor size (Arthur et al., 2012)."
effects.notes: Quoted verbatim text in 'evidence' is as rendered ('tumor counts cannot be directly compared to the original study' in the source); wording checked against the Markdown rendition of the XML. Lesions were coalescing and 'too numerous to count' in most mice, so only 10 of 24 mice could be enumerated; the direction in those was the same as the original (median 3.5 vs 2) but no statistical comparison was made and the authors state the counts cannot be directly compared. Coded inconclusive under the failure/inconclusive tiebreaker: the authors do not frame it as a failure, they frame the comparison as impossible because of the 9-week-longer experimental endpoint. An adjudicator could argue this claim was not testable at all and should get no row; I keep it because it is one of the designated replication outcomes (Figure 4A) and a directional result is reported.

effects.original_title: Intestinal inflammation targets cancer-inducing activity of the microbiota
effects.original_authors: Arthur, JC; Perez-Chanona, E; Mühlbauer, M; Tomkovich, S; Uronis, JM; Fan, TJ; Campbell, BJ; Abujamel, T; Dogan, B; Rogers, AB; Rhodes, JM; Stintzi, A; Simpson, KW; Hansen, JJ; Keku, TO; Fodor, AA; Jobin, C
effects.replication_study: Protocol 3 / Figure 3B — histological inflammation score (replication of Figure 4A-F of the original)
effects.timepoint: Mice surviving 14 weeks or more after the last AOM injection (original study assessed 18 weeks after mono-association)
effects.description: The original reported that absence of the pks island did NOT alter colonic inflammation in AOM-treated germ-free Il10-/- mice (inflammation scores: NC101 median = 4, range 4-4; NC101Δpks median = 4, range 3-4).
effects.citation_sentence: To test whether absence of the pks island reduced tumorigenic potential, but not inflammatory potential of E. coli, we attempted to independently replicate an experiment similar to the one reported in Figure 4A–F, and Supplemental Figure 10, of Arthur et al. (2012).
effects.evidence: Results and discussion (Figure 3B; Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney U = 72, p = 0.892, Cliff's d = 0.029, 95% CI [-0.28, 0.33]): "These results are confounded by the increased severity of inflammation and mortality of animals, most likely due to the experimental timing that occurred in this replication, which was longer than what occurred in the original study." and "these data are unable to address whether, under the conditions of the original study, NC101 and NC101Δ pks differ in inflammation, invasion, and neoplasia."
effects.notes: Taken on its face the replication agrees with the original's null claim (no difference in inflammation; p = 0.892), which would be a success under the null-claim rule. But the authors explicitly disown the comparison — median scores were at or near the maximum possible in both cohorts because of the 9-week-longer endpoint, 'Any differences attributable to the absence of pks would have been masked', and this comparison was excluded from the meta-analysis ('We excluded the comparisons of inflammation, invasion, and neoplasia scores since the experimental timing between the original study and this replication attempt were not the same'). Because the authors state the data cannot address the question, inconclusive. A second coder could reasonably code success here (agreement with a null claim) or treat the paper's three score comparisons as unscoreable.

effects.replication_study: Protocol 3 / Figure 3C — histological invasion score (replication of Figure 4A-F of the original)
effects.timepoint: Mice surviving 14 weeks or more after the last AOM injection (original study assessed 18 weeks after mono-association)
effects.description: The original reported that absence of the pks island resulted in a statistically significant decrease in histological invasion scores (NC101 median = 2, range 1-6; NC101Δpks median = 1, range 0-2) 18 weeks after mono-association.
effects.citation_sentence: To test whether absence of the pks island reduced tumorigenic potential, but not inflammatory potential of E. coli, we attempted to independently replicate an experiment similar to the one reported in Figure 4A–F, and Supplemental Figure 10, of Arthur et al. (2012).
effects.evidence: Results and discussion (Figure 3C; Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney U = 80, p = 0.488, Cliff's d = 0.14, 95% CI [-0.25, 0.49]): "We found that there were no substantial differences in the inflammation, invasion, or neoplasia scores between mice mono-associated with NC101 or NC101Δ pks." followed by "Thus, these results cannot be directly compared to the original study which reported that the absence of the pks island resulted in a statistically significant decrease in neoplasia scores ... and invasion scores" and "these data are unable to address whether, under the conditions of the original study, NC101 and NC101Δ pks differ in inflammation, invasion, and neoplasia."
effects.notes: A no-difference result where the original found a significant difference would normally be a failure, but the authors attribute the null to a methodological error in their own design (endpoint 9 weeks longer than the original; scores saturated near maximum in both arms), explicitly say the results cannot be compared to the original, and excluded this effect from the meta-analysis. Inconclusive under the codebook's failure/inconclusive tiebreaker and the 'substantial validity concerns' rule. A second coder could plausibly code failure.

effects.timepoint: Mice surviving 14 weeks or more after the last AOM injection (original study assessed 18 weeks after mono-association)
effects.description: The original reported that absence of the pks island resulted in a statistically significant decrease in neoplasia scores (NC101 median = 4, range 4-5; NC101Δpks median = 4, range 3-4) 18 weeks after mono-association.
effects.citation_sentence: To test whether absence of the pks island reduced tumorigenic potential, but not inflammatory potential of E. coli, we attempted to independently replicate an experiment similar to the one reported in Figure 4A–F, and Supplemental Figure 10, of Arthur et al. (2012).
effects.evidence: Results and discussion (Figure 3D; Wilcoxon-Mann-Whitney U = 72, p = 0.892, Cliff's d = 0.029, 95% CI [-0.28, 0.33]): "When considering all the mice that survived 14 weeks post-AOM treatment (5 weeks beyond the endpoint in Arthur et al., 2012), or later, the median scores for each measure were at or near the maximum possible for both cohorts (inflammation = 6; invasion = 8; neoplasia = 5)" and "since this replication attempt did not model the kinetics of the mouse model as they occurred in the original study, these data are unable to address whether, under the conditions of the original study, NC101 and NC101Δ pks differ in inflammation, invasion, and neoplasia."
effects.notes: Same reasoning as the invasion row: a null where the original was significant, but the authors disown the comparison because of the longer experimental endpoint and saturated scores, and excluded it from the meta-analysis. Inconclusive; failure is the plausible competing label.
